reason: Pale Finch's quote (NBL-017-Q1, £186, valid to 28 Feb) is on file and was received from the assigned contractor. The property matches (the only address difference is the fuller postcode form). The landlord's event-017 asks whether it can be approved from the repair budget, but it also asks for the scope and the building's response to be confirmed before booking. That is not a clear written approval of the quote, and event-007 only authorised an inspection. The building manager was asked on 12 Feb at 09:30 (event-018), under four hours before the decision time, so a reply is not overdue. Building management has asked twice to be consulted (events 5 and 13), and no work is booked (event-019). Nothing in the case reports danger: the door latches and the tenant reports no access issue (events 1, 15). The building file lists the door as fire-resisting (event-5), and the quote expressly excludes any door or fire-performance inspection. That gap does not need an escalation now, but it should go to the landlord with the approval request. I considered ROUTE_FOR_APPROVAL now. It is premature because the landlord asked for the building response first, and the 12 Feb note (event-19) already told him it is pending. Chasing Ravi is too early. Escalation is not needed because there is no conflict, danger or spend above the £300 limit. This decision would change if Ravi replies, if the landlord gives explicit written approval, or if the tenant reports the door no longer latching. In those cases I would route the quote for approval or escalate.
unknowns: Building manager's response on whether approval or specific materials/procedure are needed
Landlord's explicit written approval of the £186 quote
Door's actual condition and fire-door status (no door-set inspection done)
Whether the landlord will fund a separate door inspection
options: Wait for the building manager's reply, then route the £186 quote to the landlord
Chase Ravi Dast after 3 days if there is no reply
Ask the landlord separately about a competent door inspection for the top-edge contact
